reason: 78 children with otitis media, respiratory or urinary infections on standard antibiotic treatment. Served RR 0.5 (0.06-3.5) printed. Analysis set NOT STATED.
reviewed_note: 78 children with otitis media, respiratory or urinary infections on standard antibiotic treatment. Served RR 0.5 (0.06-3.5) printed. Analysis set NOT STATED.

population.span: Seventy-eight children (age: 5 months to 16 years) with otitis media, and/or respiratory tract infections, and/or urinary tract infections were enrolled in a double-blind randomized control trial

endpoint.span: diarrhea (> or =3 loose or watery stools/day for > or =48 h occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy)

estimate.span: Patients receiving probiotics had a similar rate of diarrhea (> or =3 loose or watery stools/day for > or =48 h occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy) as those receiving placebo (relative risk 0.5, 95% CI 0.06-3.5).

ci.span: Patients receiving probiotics had a similar rate of diarrhea (> or =3 loose or watery stools/day for > or =48 h occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy) as those receiving placebo (relative risk 0.5, 95% CI 0.06-3.5).

treatment_strategy.span: standard antibiotic treatment plus a food supplement containing 10(8) colony-forming units of B. longum, L. rhamnosus and L. plantarum (n = 40) or a placebo (n = 38) orally twice daily for the duration of antibiotic treatment.

follow_up.span: occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy

entry_population_reading.span: Seventy-eight children (age: 5 months to 16 years) with otitis media, and/or respiratory tract infections, and/or urinary tract infections were enrolled in a double-blind randomized control trial in which they received standard antibiotic treatment

analysis_set.absent_reason: Neither held abstract states whether the reported estimate was computed in an intention-to-treat or another analysis population.

entry_population.extractor_why: The enrolled children received standard antibiotic treatment, matching the question's patients receiving antibiotics; the ITT analysis designation remains unverified.

extractor_mismatch_note: The served effect and confidence interval match the reported diarrhoea endpoint. The served intention-to-treat analysis-set designation is not substantiated by either held source.
